title: The first superconducting final focus quadrupole prototype of the FCC-ee study

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states that, during warm tests, an additional step "reduced multipole errors" and that this step consisted of rotating the magnet by about 45 degrees relative to the measuring system. A rigid azimuthal rotation cannot reduce the physical magnitude of a multipole harmonic: it only rotates/mixes its normal and skew coefficients. For harmonic n, the invariant magnitude sqrt(a_n^2+b_n^2) is unchanged by a coordinate rotation. If reported errors decreased after reorientation, this indicates a coordinate/alignment, centering/feed-down, or analysis effect that must be identified and corrected; it cannot be presented as a reduction of the magnet's intrinsic multipole errors.

predicted_errors.error_location: Field-quality comparison of warm 5 A and cold 765 A measurements; abstract claim of consistency with warm tests
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper compares cold results with warm measurements while admitting that the warm measurement included an additional magnet-rotation procedure that allegedly reduced reported multipoles: "We have not repeated the extra step done at warm which reduced multipole errors." Consequently, the warm and cold results were not obtained under equivalent alignment/analysis conditions. The assertion in the abstract that cold field quality is "consistent with simulations and room temperature tests," and any inference that the cold measurements are intrinsically worse than warm measurements, is confounded by this protocol difference.

The abstract unqualifiedly claims "higher-order multipoles below 1 × 10^-4 units." The results section limits the below-one-unit statement to "the central region" and separately reports edge harmonics on the corrected side as only "below 5 units," explicitly noting a different edge normalization. The prototype deliberately retains an uncorrected edge for comparison. No measured full-length, consistently normalized integrated harmonic values are reported to establish the abstract's blanket below-1e-4 claim for the magnet as a whole; dilution of edge errors in a longer integrated magnet is asserted rather than quantified.

predicted_errors.error_location: Paragraph beginning "This validates the possibility of tuning..."
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper claims that the edge-layout approach can "remove undesired higher-order multipole content" and "can also get rid of crosstalk from the adjacent magnet in a twin aperture arrangement." The reported experiment only compares one corrected and one uncorrected edge of a single-aperture quadrupole, with residual corrected-edge harmonics described as below 5 units. No twin-aperture magnet or adjacent-aperture crosstalk measurement is reported. The demonstrated result supports reduction/tuning of edge harmonics, not removal of them or validated crosstalk cancellation.

The manuscript cites references [1]–[8], including support for the FCC-ee design, prior CCT work, paraffin-wax training claims, warm-test results, and the rotating-coil formalism, but provides no bibliography or reference entries anywhere in the supplied full text. This makes the cited claims and attribution unverifiable and requires correction.
